analysis.title: Wall Street's defensive trade is running out of steam
key_insights: XLU has rallied about 13% since early October after The Market Ear flagged it at the washout lows, when utilities were oversold, bond volatility was rising and the 10-year yield looked stretched.
The report says the setup is now stretched: XLU is near major technical resistance, its divergence from Treasuries is extreme, and defensive valuations are near levels last seen decades ago.
XLU is back near its 200-day moving average and the downtrend line in place since March. The report says this is not an ideal place to chase.
XLU has decoupled from TLT after tracking it closely since March. It has outperformed TLT by about 5 percentage points over the past 20 sessions, a 3-standard-deviation move.
GS's Privorotsky points to a large rerating in defensives, with relative multiple expansion near multi-decade highs.

With real and nominal yields still elevated, investors are paying a large premium for safety in equities. The report says equities are pricing a growth scare that the bond market has not acknowledged.

market_movers.rationale: After a 13% rally from early October, the report says risk/reward is considerably less attractive. XLU faces resistance at its 200-day moving average and the March downtrend line.

sector_views.rationale: The report says the rates relief trade worked from the lows, but after a 13% rally the setup is stretched and risk/reward is less attractive. It does not call for a short.

risk_factors: XLU is at resistance (200-day moving average and the downtrend line since March), so further upside may be limited.
The equity-bond divergence could close either way: utilities could fall back toward bonds, or bonds could price the growth scare.
Real and nominal yields remain elevated, which makes the premium paid for defensive equities harder to justify.
